In May 2022, Allscripts sold its hospital and large physician practice business (Sunrise, Paragon, TouchWorks, dbMotion) to Harris Computer / Constellation Software for ~$700M; that segment became **Altera Digital Health**. The remaining ambulatory EHR, practice management, patient engagement, and data analytics businesses were formally rebranded as **Veradigm** in January 2023.\n     9→\n    10→Veradigm has ~2,450 employees and generates approximately $585M in annual revenue across two segments: Provider (~77% of revenue, covering EHR, practice management, patient engagement, and revenue cycle management) and Payer & Life Sciences (~23%, covering data analytics and real-world evidence). The company claims over 180,000 physician users. It holds approximately 3.6% of the U.S. ambulatory EHR market — significant in the small-to-mid-size independent practice segment, though small relative to Epic (~44%).\n    11→\n    12→Veradigm has been in financial turmoil since March 2023 when it disclosed a ~$20M revenue overstatement (2021-2022), triggering an SEC investigation, executive departures, and Nasdaq delisting in February 2024. Shares now trade OTC under ticker MDRX. The company continues operating and plans to relist after completing financial restatements, targeted for 2026. The Flowsheet and Questionnaire tables may contain specialty-specific assessments, but the documentation does not describe what specialty data is captured or how custom forms/templates map to export fields. The export appears to use generic container tables (FlowsheetDefinitions, QuestionnaireRecords) that can hold specialty data, which is good for completeness but makes it hard to verify.\n   155→- **Prior authorization records**: ePrescribe has eAUTH, but the EHR export doesn't clearly include PA data. The PM export includes \"Prior Authorization Number\" as a claim field.\n   156→- **Imaging study data**: The Attachments folder includes image files, but there's no specific mention of DICOM or structured radiology data beyond chart attachments.\n   157→\n   158→### Export Format & Standards\n   159→\n   160→The Veradigm EHR uses a **proprietary JSON format** that is a direct database table export. This is a legitimate (b)(10) approach — it doesn't pretend to be FHIR and exports actual database fields with native names and types. Each JSON file maps to a named database table with documented primary keys.\n   161→\n   162→**This is a genuine (b)(10) export, not a repackaged (g)(10) FHIR API.** The export covers data domains well beyond USCDI/US Core — it includes internal database IDs, audit fields, flowsheet data, questionnaire responses, risk scores, scanned documents, and practice-specific metadata that would never appear in a standardized FHIR API.\n   163→\n   164→Relationships between entities are expressed through foreign key fields (PatientID, EncounterId, ContactId, etc.) appearing across tables. A developer could reconstruct the patient record, though the lack of formal relationship documentation adds friction.\n   165→\n   166→### Documentation Quality\n   167→\n   168→**Strong aspects:**\n   169→- Field-level documentation with descriptions, data types, and database table names\n   170→- Clear folder hierarchy documentation with screenshots\n   171→- Password protection and extraction instructions\n   172→- 89-page depth for the EHR export alone\n   173→- Practice Management appendix with exhaustive claim field listings\n   174→- Veradigm View has 87 entity pages with 1,194 fields\n   175→\n   176→**Weaknesses:**\n   177→- Only version 1 (Nov 2023) for the EHR — no updates in 2+ years despite ongoing product development\n   178→- No sample export files or example JSON/TSV data\n   179→- No machine-readable schema files (JSON Schema, XSD, etc.)\n   180→- No explicit documentation of relationships between tables (foreign keys implied but not formally specified)\n   181→- No value set documentation — fields like PatientMaritalStatus, Race, Ethnicity are VARCHAR(255) with no enumeration of allowed values\n   182→- The documentation references \"Veradigm EHR 23.4 and higher\" but the certified version is 26 — unclear if v1 documentation covers changes in versions 24-26\n   183→\n   184→### Structure & Completeness\n   185→\n   186→Field-level granularity is high — each table has field names, descriptions, and SQL data types. However:\n   187→- No cardinality documentation (required vs. optional)\n   188→- No value set definitions for coded fields\n   189→- No explicit foreign key/relationship documentation\n   190→- No change history beyond initial publication\n   191→- The Veradigm View documentation (87 entities, 1,194 fields) is more granular than the EHR export (43 JSON files), reflecting different product architectures\n   192→\n   193→### Overall Assessment\n   194→\n   195→Veradigm has done genuine (b)(10) work. The EHR export is a real database-level export with password-protected ZIP files containing the patient's clinical record in JSON format, plus actual documents, images, scanned documents, and transcriptions. This is not a FHIR API repackaging.\n   196→\n   197→The breadth across five products is notable — when a customer uses the full Veradigm suite (EHR + PM + ePrescribe + FMH), the combined exports cover clinical data, billing/claims, prescriptions, and patient portal data. This is more comprehensive than many vendors.\n   198→\n   199→The main gaps are in documentation maintenance (only v1 from Nov 2023 for the core EHR) and missing data quality metadata (no value sets, no cardinality, no sample data). Each patient ZIP has four folders:\n- **Attachments** — images, documents, voice notes (jpg, gif, tif, png, wav, mp3, pdf, doc, xls, ppt, etc.)\n- **Scanned Documents** — TIF files from Input Manager scanning\n- **Transcriptions** — RTF files of transcriptions\n- **Discrete Data** — JSON files organized by clinical domain\n\nThe Discrete Data folder contains **43 JSON files** across these clinical domains:\n- **Demographics**: Demographics.json, PatientConsent.json, PatientContacts.json, PatientPhysicians.json\n- **History**: HistoryDiagnosis.json, HistoryMedication.json (includes implantable devices)\n- **Vitals**: Vitals.json\n- **Diagnosis**: Diagnosis.json\n- **Medications**: Medications.json, AdminMedications.json, RxOutputSummary.json\n- **Procedures**: Procedures.json, ProceduresResult.json\n- **Lab Orders**: LabOrders.json, LabResults.json\n- **Referrals**: Referrals.json\n- **Flowsheet**: FlowsheetDefinitions.json\n- **Risk Management**: PatientRiskScore.json\n- **Contact**: ContactData.json, ContactNotes.json\n- **Encounter**: Encounter.json, EncounterAssessment.json, EncounterPlan.json, HpiData.json, HpiDataNotes.json, ChartAddendum.json\n- **Immunization**: ImmunizationRecord.json, ImmunizationAddendum.json, ImmunizationVIS.json\n- **Message**: SavedMessages.json, SavedMessageResults.json, SavedWebMessages.json\n- **Questionnaire**: QuestionnaireRecords.json, QuestionnaireRecordResult.json, QuestionnaireRecordQuestionAnswer.json\n- **Care Plans**: PatientCarePlans.json, PatientCarePlanEncounters.json, PatientGoals.json, PatientGoalBarriers.json, PatientAchieveGoals.json, PatientHealthConcerns.json\n- **Additional files**: NoteAndAttachmentDetails.json, ScannedDocuments.json, Transcriptions.json, ChartAttachments.json\n\nEach JSON file maps directly to a named EHR database table with field-level documentation including field names, descriptions, and SQL data types (VARCHAR, Integer, DateTime, etc.). The documentation is a genuine database-level data dictionary.\n\n### Veradigm ePrescribe Export (TSV, Nov 2023)\n\nExports as **TSV (tab-separated values) files** in ZIP format. Contains 7 files per patient:\n- Allergies.tsv, Demographics.tsv, Diagnosis.tsv, Historical Medications.tsv, Insurance.tsv, Prescriptions.tsv, Read Me.txt\n\nEach TSV file is documented with database table names, primary keys, field names, descriptions, and SQL data types.\n\n### Veradigm Practice Management Export (JSON, V2 May 2024)\n\nExports patient **financial/billing data** as JSON. Documents a claims-oriented JSON structure with:\n- Practice and patient identification\n- Voucher-level billing data (charges, payments, adjustments, balances)\n- Provider, referring provider, responsible party, billing provider\n- Claim information fields (prior authorization, condition codes, occurrence codes, value codes)\n- Service-level details (procedure codes, descriptions, units, fees, modifiers, diagnoses)\n- Payment transactions\n- Specialty appendices for ambulance, drug, anesthesia, and dental information\n\n### FollowMyHealth Export (FHIR R4 JSON, V2 Feb 2024)\n\nExports as a **FHIR R4 Bundle in JSON format** (plus raw documents/images) in a ZIP. Explicitly states: \"This is not an implementation of SMART/HL7 Bulk Data Access (Flat FHIR). FollowMyHealth is not currently using any FHIR Profile, such as US Core in this implementation.\"\n\nSupported FHIR resources: Account, AllergyIntolerance, Appointment, Bundle, Communication, Condition, DiagnosticReport, DocumentReference, Encounter, FamilyMemberHistory, Immunization, Invoice, Medication, MedicationRequest, Observation, Patient, Practitioner, Procedure.\n\nUses custom FHIR extensions for allergy status, health condition status, procedure status, and family member history. FMH is a Personal Health Record (PHR) that aggregates data from connected source EHRs.\n\n### Veradigm View Export (TSV, V6 Jan 2026)\n\nThe most recently updated documentation. Exports as **TSV files** covering **87 entity types** with **1,194 documented fields**. Categories include:\n- Demographics (communication settings, contacts, demographics, ethnicity, gender identity, guarantor, occupation, race, tribal affiliation)\n- Clinical (advance directives, allergies, conditions, diagnoses, encounters, family history, goals, health concerns, healthcare devices, immunizations, medications, prescriptions, procedures, questionnaires, referrals, restrictions, risk scores, smoking status, vitals/observations)\n- Labs (lab orders, order items, order documents, results, result tests/observations, result notes, specimens)\n- Billing/Insurance (insurances, insurance eligibilities, superbills, superbill diagnoses, superbill events, superbill insurances, superbill procedures)\n- Messaging (messages, message attachments, message recipients)\n- Administrative (care teams, facilities, pharmacies, providers, users)\n\n**Important**: The View documentation pages reference \"Practice Fusion EHR\" in entity descriptions. Veradigm acquired Practice Fusion in 2018 and appears to have rebranded it as \"Veradigm View.\" This is a separate product from Veradigm EHR (formerly Allscripts Professional).\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\n**Veradigm EHR** (the certified product, CHPL 11763):\n\n**Clearly covered:**\n- Demographics, contacts, consent (comprehensive — 60+ fields)\n- Problem lists / diagnoses (active and historical, with ICD/SNOMED coding)\n- Medications (active, historical, administered, Rx summaries)\n- Vitals\n- Lab orders and results\n- Procedures and procedure results\n- Immunizations (including VIS records and addenda)\n- Encounters (with assessment plans, HPI data, addenda)\n- Care plans, goals, health concerns\n- Referrals\n- Flowsheet data (custom clinical worksheets)\n- Clinical notes (via Transcriptions, ChartAddendum, encounter notes)\n- Documents and attachments (images, scanned docs, voice notes)\n- Messages (patient/provider messaging)\n- Questionnaires (with question/answer detail)\n- Risk management scores\n- Implantable device data\n\n**Covered via companion products (PM and ePrescribe):**\n- Billing/claims data (via Practice Management export — vouchers, charges, payments, procedure codes, modifiers)\n- Insurance information (via ePrescribe export)\n- Detailed prescriptions (via ePrescribe export)\n\n**Potentially missing or not clearly documented:**\n- **Specialty-specific clinical data**: The product supports \"nearly every medical specialty\" with preloaded templates. The Flowsheet and Questionnaire tables may contain specialty-specific assessments, but the documentation does not describe what specialty data is captured or how custom forms/templates map to export fields. The export appears to use generic container tables (FlowsheetDefinitions, QuestionnaireRecords) that can hold specialty data, which is good for completeness but makes it hard to verify.\n- **Prior authorization records**: ePrescribe has eAUTH, but the EHR export doesn't clearly include PA data. The PM export includes \"Prior Authorization Number\" as a claim field.\n- **Imaging study data**: The Attachments folder includes image files, but there's no specific mention of DICOM or structured radiology data beyond chart attachments.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe Veradigm EHR uses a **proprietary JSON format** that is a direct database table export. This is a legitimate (b)(10) approach — it doesn't pretend to be FHIR and exports actual database fields with native names and types. Each JSON file maps to a named database table with documented primary keys.\n\n**This is a genuine (b)(10) export, not a repackaged (g)(10) FHIR API.** The export covers data domains well beyond USCDI/US Core — it includes internal database IDs, audit fields, flowsheet data, questionnaire responses, risk scores, scanned documents, and practice-specific metadata that would never appear in a standardized FHIR API.\n\nRelationships between entities are expressed through foreign key fields (PatientID, EncounterId, ContactId, etc.) appearing across tables. A developer could reconstruct the patient record, though the lack of formal relationship documentation adds friction.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Strong aspects:**\n- Field-level documentation with descriptions, data types, and database table names\n- Clear folder hierarchy documentation with screenshots\n- Password protection and extraction instructions\n- 89-page depth for the EHR export alone\n- Practice Management appendix with exhaustive claim field listings\n- Veradigm View has 87 entity pages with 1,194 fields\n\n**Weaknesses:**\n- Only version 1 (Nov 2023) for the EHR — no updates in 2+ years despite ongoing product development\n- No sample export files or example JSON/TSV data\n- No machine-readable schema files (JSON Schema, XSD, etc.)\n- No explicit documentation of relationships between tables (foreign keys implied but not formally specified)\n- No value set documentation — fields like PatientMaritalStatus, Race, Ethnicity are VARCHAR(255) with no enumeration of allowed values\n- The documentation references \"Veradigm EHR 23.4 and higher\" but the certified version is 26 — unclear if v1 documentation covers changes in versions 24-26\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nField-level granularity is high — each table has field names, descriptions, and SQL data types. However:\n- No cardinality documentation (required vs. optional)\n- No value set definitions for coded fields\n- No explicit foreign key/relationship documentation\n- No change history beyond initial publication\n- The Veradigm View documentation (87 entities, 1,194 fields) is more granular than the EHR export (43 JSON files), reflecting different product architectures\n\n### Overall Assessment\n\nVeradigm has done genuine (b)(10) work. The EHR export is a real database-level export with password-protected ZIP files containing the patient's clinical record in JSON format, plus actual documents, images, scanned documents, and transcriptions. This is not a FHIR API repackaging.\n\nThe breadth across five products is notable — when a customer uses the full Veradigm suite (EHR + PM + ePrescribe + FMH), the combined exports cover clinical data, billing/claims, prescriptions, and patient portal data. This is more comprehensive than many vendors.\n\nThe main gaps are in documentation maintenance (only v1 from Nov 2023 for the core EHR) and missing data quality metadata (no value sets, no cardinality, no sample data). A developer could implement an import from this documentation but would need significant discovery work around coded values and entity relationships.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://veradigm.com/legal/onc-reg-compliance/\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: one_click (EHI section visible in page source, direct PDF links)\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n\nNone significant. Veradigm Inc.\nThis page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n\fPreliminary considerations\nAbout this guide\nRead this guide if you requested patient data from a practice that uses Veradigm® EHR, and the practice fulfilled your\nrequest with files generated from the EHR’s Electronic Health Information (EHI) Export tool. This guide gives you\ninformation and links to additional resources for integrating the data into your organization’s software.\n\n\nExtracting from the .zip files\nBecause the Veradigm EHR EHI Export tool packages data in .zip files, you probably received at least one .zip file from the\npractice.\n\nTo unzip the file, use a third-party file archiver program that supports password protection, such as WinZip, WinRAR, or 7zip.\nYou must enter a password (provided by the practice) to extract the contents. The file extraction feature in Microsoft®\nWindows® Explorer does not support password protection, and will not work to unzip the file.\n\nThe file contents are one or more other .zip files, each of which corresponds with a single patient chart. In the following\nexample, the top-level .zip file from Practice ABC contains seven .zip files for seven different patients; each file is named with a\ncombination of the patient’s EHR ID and export request number. (Be aware that different Veradigm EHR practices might have\ndifferent naming conventions.)\n\n\n\n\nNovember 9, 2023 | Veradigm® EHR                                                                                                   5\nVersion 1 documentation for Veradigm EHR EHI Export output formatting\nCopyright © 2023 | Veradigm Inc.\nThis page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n\fFigure 1: Example patient .zip files (viewed in archiver program WinRAR)\n\n\n\n\n                          Note: The example above displays patient .zip files in a window of the file archiver\n                          program WinRAR. If you use a different archiver program, the .zip file icons will be\n                          different, and the options for extracting and working with files will be different.\n\nTo extract the contents of an individual patient .zip file, you do not need to supply a password.\n\n\n\nNovember 9, 2023 | Veradigm® EHR                                                                                        6\nVersion 1 documentation for Veradigm EHR EHI Export output formatting\nCopyright © 2023 | Veradigm Inc.\nThis page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n\fFolder hierarchy of a patient .zip file\nEach patient .zip file contains four top-level folders:\n        Attachments\n        Scanned Documents\n        Transcriptions\n        Discrete Data\n\n\n\nAttachments folder\nThis top-level folder contains images, documents, and voice notes that are associated with the patient’s chart. File types can\ninclude:\n      .jpg, .gif, .tif, and .png\n      .wav and .mp3\n      PDFs\n      Microsoft® Word® files\n      Microsoft® Excel® files\n      Microsoft® PowerPoint® files\n      And many more\n\nIf no attachments exist for a patient, the folder will simply be empty.\n\n\n\nScanned Documents folder\nThis top-level folder also contains documents that are associated with the patient’s chart. Called scanned documents, they\ndiffer from other files saved to a patient chart because they originated as hard-copy documents that were scanned into the\nEHR through a component called Input Manager. All scanned documents are of file type .tif.\n\nNote that multi-page scanned documents are saved as a sequence of .tif files, each with the same numerical prefix.                                                                                      ®\n   155→Read this guide if you requested patient data from a practice that uses FollowMyHealth , and the\n   156→practice fulfilled your request with files generated from the FollowMyHealth Electronic Health\n   157→Information (EHI) Export tool or if the patient or the patient's authorized individual performed an\n   158→EHI export from within the patient's account in the FollowMyHealth Personal Health Record. This\n   159→guide provides information on the data included in the export documentation and the format of the\n   160→data.\n   161→There might be multiple versions of this EHI Export Data Guide available. Be sure to use the latest\n   162→version of the guide corresponding to when the EHI Export is performed. All versions of this guide\n   163→are available at the following location under the “EHI Export Documentation” menu option:\n   164→https://veradigm.com/legal/onc-reg-compliance/.\n   165→The output of the EHI Export tool includes a JSON formatted file, which includes a link to the\n   166→appropriate version of this EHI Export documentation. This link is found near the top of the JSON\n   167→file in the “link” section under “relation”:“service-doc”, similar to the following example.\n   168→\n   169→\n   170→\n   171→\n   172→Note in this example the version referenced at the end of the URL: “.../v1”. This will be incremented\n   173→each time the guide is updated.\n   174→As of this writing, the latest version of the guide is:\n   175→https://fhir.followmyhealth.com/documentation/EHIExportDocumentation/v2\n   176→\n   177→            Note: Protecting the patient’s health data is the responsibility of all entities\n   178→            involved in the transmission and downloading of their data. Once the file\n   179→            is retrieved and downloaded, it is the responsibility of the client, the patient,\n   180→            or the patient's authorized individual performing the download to follow all\n   181→            applicable HIPAA and Security and Privacy rules to protect the patient’s\n   182→            data.\n   183→\n   184→\n   185→February 28, 2024 | FollowMyHealth®                                                                                         7\n   186→EHI Export Data Guide Version 2.0\n   187→Copyright © 2024 | Veradigm LLC\n   188→This page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n   189→\fExtracting the .zip files\n   190→Because the FollowMyHealth EHI Export tool packages data for each patient in a single .zip file,\n   191→you should receive at least one .zip file from the practice.\n   192→To unzip the file, use a third-party file archiver program , such as WinZip, WinRAR, or 7zip to\n   193→extract the contents.\n   194→The contents of the .zip file for each patient include a JSON file containing all of the patient data,\n   195→plus other documents and images associated with the patient. The .zip file and the JSON file are\n   196→named with the patient's unique FMH ID.\n   197→Here is an example of the .zip file contents. Note the JSON file is included, along with additional\n   198→documents and images associated with the patient.\n   199→\n   200→\n   201→\n   202→\n   203→8                                                                                          FollowMyHealth® | February 28, 2024\n   204→                                                                                              EHI Export Data Guide Version 2.0\n   205→                                                                                               Copyright © 2024 | Veradigm LLC\n   206→           This page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n   207→\fFiltering data included in the export\n   208→The exporting of electronic health information may be performed by a patient or their authorized\n   209→individual, or by a representative from the client organization on behalf of a patient. The Electronic\n   210→Health Information exported from FollowMyHealth by the client from within the Dashboard, or by\n   211→directly calling the FMH FHIR API Service, will be limited to the data originating from the client’s\n   212→source electronic health record.\n   213→\n   214→\n   215→February 28, 2024 | FollowMyHealth®                                                                                     9\n   216→EHI Export Data Guide Version 2.0\n   217→Copyright © 2024 | Veradigm LLC\n   218→This page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n   219→\fElectronic Health Information exported from FollowMyHealth by the patient or their authorized\n   220→individual from the patient's account in the Personal Health Record will include all data stored in\n   221→FollowMyHealth from all sources.\n   222→\n   223→\n   224→\n   225→\n   226→10                                                                                         FollowMyHealth® | February 28, 2024\n   227→                                                                                              EHI Export Data Guide Version 2.0\n   228→                                                                                               Copyright © 2024 | Veradigm LLC\n   229→           This page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n   230→\fExport Format\n   231→FollowMyHealth outputs a single .zip file for each patient which contains a FHIR R4 Bundle in\n   232→JSON format, as well as the raw documents and images associated with the patient. This is not\n   233→an implementation of SMART/HL7 Bulk Data Access (Flat FHIR). FollowMyHealth is not currently\n   234→using any FHIR Profile, such as US Core in this implementation. In some cases the internal\n   235→FollowMyHealth data structures might not map well into existing FHIR resource types or value\n   236→sets. In these cases, extensions are used to capture the data.\n   237→\n   238→\n   239→\n   240→Common Fields\n   241→ID\n   242→       The FollowMyHealth GUID (Globally Unique IDentifier) for the object.\n   243→\n   244→Identifier\n   245→      The collection of IDs from the source (the EHR application) for the object.\n   246→\n   247→Meta > LastUpdated\n   248→     Last time the object was modified.\n   249→\n   250→Note\n   251→       Used to store plaintext fields on a FollowMyHealth object. If the object has a Comments\n   252→       field, this is what will be used.\n   253→\n   254→\n   255→\n   256→General Exceptions\n   257→As FollowMyHealth is a Personal Health Record (PHR), and not an electronic health record (EHR)\n   258→application, the data that is stored is a best effort to capture everything in the source EHR\n   259→application, Practice Management (PM) system, and so on.\n   260→Exception: FHIR expects the Display value to match the official display values for the code system.\n   261→FollowMyHealth uses the name stored on the item instead, which might or might not match the\n   262→official code system display value.\n   263→\n   264→\n   265→\n   266→\n   267→February 28, 2024 | FollowMyHealth®                                                                                     11\n   268→EHI Export Data Guide Version 2.0\n   269→Copyright © 2024 | Veradigm LLC\n   270→This page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n   271→\fFollowing is an example where this exception occurs in the Condition resource:\n   272→\n   273→     Code: J18.9\n   274→     Code system: ICD-10 CM\n   275→     Display: pneumonia\n   276→\n   277→\n   278→FHIR expects the description to be displayed as pneumonia, unspecified organism, but\n   279→FMH displays the description (pneumonia) received from the source system.\n   280→\n   281→\n   282→\n   283→Data Exceptions\n   284→Any data that is visible in the FollowMyHealth account but not exported will be found under a Data\n   285→Exceptions section. This data is excluded since it is not stored in FollowMyHealth. These are\n   286→items that are sourced from a third party or directly from the source system (such as an EHR\n   287→application) during login or page navigation.\n   288→\n   289→\n   290→\n   291→Extensions\n   292→In some cases the internal FollowMyHealth data structures might not map well into existing FHIR\n   293→resource types or value sets, or there might not be an existing field in the FHIR resource to capture\n   294→FollowMyHealth data. In these cases, extensions are used to capture and present the data in the\n   295→JSON output file. Further information regarding extensions are discussed under the resource types\n   296→for which they are being used.\n   297→\n   298→\n   299→\n   300→\n   301→12        ®\nRead this guide if you requested patient data from a practice that uses FollowMyHealth , and the\npractice fulfilled your request with files generated from the FollowMyHealth Electronic Health\nInformation (EHI) Export tool or if the patient or the patient's authorized individual performed an\nEHI export from within the patient's account in the FollowMyHealth Personal Health Record. This\nguide provides information on the data included in the export documentation and the format of the\ndata.\nThere might be multiple versions of this EHI Export Data Guide available. Be sure to use the latest\nversion of the guide corresponding to when the EHI Export is performed. All versions of this guide\nare available at the following location under the “EHI Export Documentation” menu option:\nhttps://veradigm.com/legal/onc-reg-compliance/.\nThe output of the EHI Export tool includes a JSON formatted file, which includes a link to the\nappropriate version of this EHI Export documentation. This link is found near the top of the JSON\nfile in the “link” section under “relation”:“service-doc”, similar to the following example.\n\n\n\n\nNote in this example the version referenced at the end of the URL: “.../v1”. This will be incremented\neach time the guide is updated.\nAs of this writing, the latest version of the guide is:\nhttps://fhir.followmyhealth.com/documentation/EHIExportDocumentation/v2\n\n            Note: Protecting the patient’s health data is the responsibility of all entities\n            involved in the transmission and downloading of their data. Once the file\n            is retrieved and downloaded, it is the responsibility of the client, the patient,\n            or the patient's authorized individual performing the download to follow all\n            applicable HIPAA and Security and Privacy rules to protect the patient’s\n            data.\n\n\nFebruary 28, 2024 | FollowMyHealth®                                                                                         7\nEHI Export Data Guide Version 2.0\nCopyright © 2024 | Veradigm LLC\nThis page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n\fExtracting the .zip files\nBecause the FollowMyHealth EHI Export tool packages data for each patient in a single .zip file,\nyou should receive at least one .zip file from the practice.\nTo unzip the file, use a third-party file archiver program , such as WinZip, WinRAR, or 7zip to\nextract the contents.\nThe contents of the .zip file for each patient include a JSON file containing all of the patient data,\nplus other documents and images associated with the patient. The .zip file and the JSON file are\nnamed with the patient's unique FMH ID.\nHere is an example of the .zip file contents. Note the JSON file is included, along with additional\ndocuments and images associated with the patient.\n\n\n\n\n8                                                                                          FollowMyHealth® | February 28, 2024\n                                                                                              EHI Export Data Guide Version 2.0\n                                                                                               Copyright © 2024 | Veradigm LLC\n           This page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n\fFiltering data included in the export\nThe exporting of electronic health information may be performed by a patient or their authorized\nindividual, or by a representative from the client organization on behalf of a patient. The Electronic\nHealth Information exported from FollowMyHealth by the client from within the Dashboard, or by\ndirectly calling the FMH FHIR API Service, will be limited to the data originating from the client’s\nsource electronic health record.\n\n\nFebruary 28, 2024 | FollowMyHealth®                                                                                     9\nEHI Export Data Guide Version 2.0\nCopyright © 2024 | Veradigm LLC\nThis page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n\fElectronic Health Information exported from FollowMyHealth by the patient or their authorized\nindividual from the patient's account in the Personal Health Record will include all data stored in\nFollowMyHealth from all sources.\n\n\n\n\n10                                                                                         FollowMyHealth® | February 28, 2024\n                                                                                              EHI Export Data Guide Version 2.0\n                                                                                               Copyright © 2024 | Veradigm LLC\n           This page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n\fExport Format\nFollowMyHealth outputs a single .zip file for each patient which contains a FHIR R4 Bundle in\nJSON format, as well as the raw documents and images associated with the patient. This is not\nan implementation of SMART/HL7 Bulk Data Access (Flat FHIR). FollowMyHealth is not currently\nusing any FHIR Profile, such as US Core in this implementation. In some cases the internal\nFollowMyHealth data structures might not map well into existing FHIR resource types or value\nsets. In these cases, extensions are used to capture the data.\n\n\n\nCommon Fields\nID\n       The FollowMyHealth GUID (Globally Unique IDentifier) for the object.\n\nIdentifier\n      The collection of IDs from the source (the EHR application) for the object.\n\nMeta > LastUpdated\n     Last time the object was modified.\n\nNote\n       Used to store plaintext fields on a FollowMyHealth object. If the object has a Comments\n       field, this is what will be used.\n\n\n\nGeneral Exceptions\nAs FollowMyHealth is a Personal Health Record (PHR), and not an electronic health record (EHR)\napplication, the data that is stored is a best effort to capture everything in the source EHR\napplication, Practice Management (PM) system, and so on.\nException: FHIR expects the Display value to match the official display values for the code system.\nFollowMyHealth uses the name stored on the item instead, which might or might not match the\nofficial code system display value.\n\n\n\n\nFebruary 28, 2024 | FollowMyHealth®                                                                                     11\nEHI Export Data Guide Version 2.0\nCopyright © 2024 | Veradigm LLC\nThis page contains Veradigm proprietary information and is not to be duplicated or disclosed to unauthorized persons.\n\fFollowing is an example where this exception occurs in the Condition resource:\n\n     Code: J18.9\n     Code system: ICD-10 CM\n     Display: pneumonia\n\n\nFHIR expects the description to be displayed as pneumonia, unspecified organism, but\nFMH displays the description (pneumonia) received from the source system.\n\n\n\nData Exceptions\nAny data that is visible in the FollowMyHealth account but not exported will be found under a Data\nExceptions section. This data is excluded since it is not stored in FollowMyHealth. These are\nitems that are sourced from a third party or directly from the source system (such as an EHR\napplication) during login or page navigation.\n\n\n\nExtensions\nIn some cases the internal FollowMyHealth data structures might not map well into existing FHIR\nresource types or value sets, or there might not be an existing field in the FHIR resource to capture\nFollowMyHealth data. In these cases, extensions are used to capture and present the data in the\nJSON output file. Further information regarding extensions are discussed under the resource types\nfor which they are being used.\n\n\n\n\n12 Export Mechanics\n\nVeradigm provides separate export mechanisms for each product component:\n\n**Veradigm EHR (core clinical data):**\n- **Format**: JSON files organized in clinical domain folders, plus raw attachments/documents/transcriptions\n- **Packaging**: Password-protected ZIP containing per-patient sub-ZIPs\n- **Mechanism**: EHI Export tool within the EHR application (UI-driven)\n- **Scope**: Single-patient or multi-patient export\n- **Access**: Practice initiates export; patient receives ZIP + password\n\n**Veradigm Practice Management (billing data):**\n- **Format**: Hierarchical JSON (single file per patient)\n- **Mechanism**: Not explicitly documented; described as \"EHI data export file\"\n- **Scope**: Per-patient financial/billing data\n- **Note**: PM is \"non ONC certified\" per the compliance page but provides separate EHI documentation\n\n**Veradigm ePrescribe (prescribing data):**\n- **Format**: TSV files in ZIP\n- **Mechanism**: Health Information Export tool within ePrescribe\n- **Scope**: Per-patient; supports single or multi-patient selection\n\n**FollowMyHealth (patient portal data):**\n- **Format**: FHIR R4 Bundle in JSON + raw documents/images in ZIP\n- **Mechanism**: Export from FMH Dashboard (by practice) or by patient from their PHR account\n- **Scope**: Per-patient; practice-initiated exports limited to data from that practice's EHR; patient-initiated exports include all sources\n- **Note**: Explicitly states \"This is not an implementation of SMART/HL7 Bulk Data Access (Flat FHIR)\"\n\n**Veradigm View / Practice Fusion (separate EHR):**\n- **Format**: TSV files\n- **Mechanism**: Not documented in the artifacts reviewed\n- **Scope**: 87 entity types across demographics, clinical, labs, billing, messaging, administrative domains\n\n**Bulk export capability**: Not explicitly documented as a single \"bulk export all patients\" mechanism. The EHR export supports multi-patient selection. No mention of fees or access constraints.\n\n## 4. Export Content: What's In It\n\n### Combined scope across all products\n\nAcross all five products, the Veradigm suite documents **169 entities** with **2,938 total fields**. Documentation quality is exceptional: 99.9% of fields have descriptions and 100% have data types.\n\n### 4a. |\n\nThe export also includes the actual binary files (images, scanned documents, transcriptions) in separate folders, not just metadata references.\n\n### 4b. Veradigm Practice Management\n\nThe PM export documents a hierarchical JSON structure for patient billing/financial data with **75 core fields** covering:\n- Practice and patient identification\n- Voucher-level billing data (charges, payments, adjustments, balances)\n- Provider, referring provider, responsible party, billing provider details\n- Service-level details (procedure codes, descriptions, units, fees, modifiers, diagnoses)\n- Payment transactions (date, insurance, transaction type, amount, transfers)\n\nPlus **317 appendix fields** covering possible values for:\n- **Claim information** (218 fields): prior authorization, condition codes 1-7, occurrence codes 1-8, value codes 1-12, diagnosis codes, procedure codes, employer info, scan regions, outgoing referrals, EPSDT fields, and more\n- **Ailment information** (51 fields): case type, disability dates, hospitalization dates, pregnancy-related, EPSDT referral codes\n- **Ambulance information** (21 fields): transport codes, pick-up addresses, stretcher/emergency indicators\n- **Drug information** (13 fields): NDC codes, lot numbers, unit pricing, lab results\n- **Anesthesia information** (12 fields): start/stop times, base units, CRNA details, related procedures\n- **Dental information** (2 fields): tooth/quadrant, surface\n\n### 4c. Veradigm ePrescribe\n\nThe ePrescribe export documents 6 TSV files with **263 fields** total:\n- **Demographics.tsv** (46 fields): patient info, pharmacy preferences (retail, mail order, other), clinical flags\n- **Allergies.tsv** (12 fields): medication and medication class allergies with RxNorm codes\n- **Diagnosis.tsv** (9 fields): ICD-9, ICD-10, SNOMED codes\n- **Historical Medications.tsv** (78 fields): comprehensive prescription details with drug checking flags, PBM card info, pharmacy details, provider credentials\n- **Insurance.tsv** (40 fields): PBM data, card holder information, formulary IDs, coverage details\n- **Prescriptions.tsv** (78 fields): active prescriptions with same level of detail as historical\n\n### 4d. It is a separate product from Veradigm EHR (Practice Fusion rebranded), but its inclusion on the same compliance page reflects the integrated suite approach.\n\n## 5. Coverage Assessment\n\n### 5a. What the vendor covers (bottom-up)\n\n**Veradigm EHR** covers the core clinical data comprehensively:\n- **Demographics** (124 fields across 4 tables): exceptionally detailed including multiple name variants (preferred, former, birth), multiple sex/gender fields (birth sex, medical sex, administrative sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, preferred pronouns), organ donor status, employment, VIP indicator, confidentiality codes.\n- **Medications** (100 fields across 3 tables): active prescriptions with 58 fields including local vs. mail-order pharmacy details, sample drug tracking, MAR records with injection sites and lot numbers.\n- **Encounter** (94 fields across 7 tables): encounters, assessments, plans, HPI data, addenda, accompanied-by records.\n- **History** (87 fields across 3 tables): historical diagnoses, historical medications, implantable devices with UDI/DI codes.\n- **Messages** (72 fields across 3 tables): saved messages, web messages, and message results.\n- **Immunization** (59 fields across 4 tables): immunization records, VIS editions, forecast, and addenda.\n- **Additional Files** (67 fields across 4 tables plus actual files): scanned documents, transcriptions, chart attachments with metadata.\n\n**Practice Management** adds deep billing coverage:\n- 75 core fields covering the full voucher-to-payment lifecycle\n- 218 claim information fields covering institutional, professional, and specialty billing\n- Specialty appendices for ambulance, anesthesia, dental, and drug billing\n\n**Combined across the suite**, the strongest areas are:\n1. **Billing/insurance** — PM provides extensive claim-level detail; View has 12 billing entities with 286 fields; ePrescribe adds 40 insurance fields\n2. **Medications/prescriptions** — Three products cover active prescriptions, historical medications, administered medications, and prescription transactions\n3. **Demographics** — All products include patient demographics at varying depths\n4. **Clinical notes/documents** — EHR exports actual files (images, scanned docs, transcriptions, voice notes) plus metadata\n\n### 5b. The data should still be exported, but without specialty-specific documentation, it's hard to verify coverage.\n\n2. **Prior authorization records**: The ePrescribe product has eAUTH for electronic prior authorization, but no dedicated prior authorization entity appears in the EHR export. The PM export includes \"Prior Authorization Number\" as a claim field.\n\n3. **Structured imaging data**: No dedicated radiology or DICOM entities. Imaging data appears to come through as attachments and procedure results.\n\n4. **Patient-generated data from FollowMyHealth**: Remote monitoring device data is mentioned in product features but not specifically documented as an exported data type beyond FMH's Observation resource.\n\nThese are relatively minor gaps for an ambulatory EHR. The core clinical, billing, messaging, and document data are well-covered.\n\n## 6. Documentation Quality\n\n**Strengths:**\n- **Field-level documentation is excellent**: 99.9% of fields across all products have human-readable descriptions (2,935 of 2,938 fields). 100% have data types.\n- **Database-level transparency**: EHR export documentation names the actual database table and primary key for each JSON file, enabling developers to understand the data model\n- **SQL types provided**: VARCHAR(255), Integer, DateTime, etc. — not just \"string\" or \"text\"\n- **Multiple format options**: JSON (EHR, PM), TSV (ePrescribe, View), FHIR R4 (FMH) — all documented\n- **Versioning**: View documentation has been updated 6 times (v1 Apr 2025 through v6 Jan 2026); PM and FMH each have v2 revisions\n- **FHIR extension definitions**: FMH provides machine-readable StructureDefinitions, CodeSystems, and ValueSets for custom extensions\n\n**Weaknesses:**\n- **EHR documentation is dated**: Only v1 from November 2023 despite the product being certified at version 26 in December 2025. The documentation references \"Veradigm EHR 23.4 and higher\" — 2+ years of product updates are undocumented.\n- **No sample data**: None of the products provide sample export files or example records\n- **No machine-readable schema**: No JSON Schema, XSD, or other parseable schema definition — just PDF and HTML documentation\n- **No explicit relationship documentation**: Foreign keys between tables (PatientID, EncounterId, ContactId) are implied by field descriptions but not formally specified\n- **No value set definitions**: Coded fields like PatientMaritalStatus, Race, Ethnicity are documented as VARCHAR(255) with no enumeration of allowed values. The asterisk convention \"(*) means Other\" appears in some fields but many coded fields have no value sets.\n- **Five separate export mechanisms**: A receiving system must implement five different format parsers (JSON, TSV, FHIR R4) to consume the full patient record across all products\n\n**Could a developer build an import?** Yes, with significant effort. The field-level documentation is sufficient to understand the data model. The main challenges would be: (1) handling five different formats, (2) discovering value sets empirically, and (3) resolving relationships between tables across products.\n\n## 7. Overall Assessment\n\n### Classification\n\n**Axis 1 — Coverage breadth: Comprehensive**\n\nThis is one of the most comprehensive EHI export documentation suites among ambulatory EHR vendors. The combined documentation covers:\n- 169 entities with 2,938 fields across 5 products\n- All major clinical domains (demographics, problems, medications, labs, vitals, immunizations, procedures, encounters, care plans)\n- Billing and claims data at a deep level (PM export with 392 fields including specialty billing appendices)\n- Insurance with PBM detail (ePrescribe Insurance.tsv with 40 fields)\n- Patient communications (45-field message table, web messages, FMH Communication resource)\n- Actual binary files (images, scanned documents, transcriptions) — not just metadata\n- Patient portal data (FMH FHIR export with 18 resource types)\n- Questionnaires and flowsheets (generic containers that capture specialty data)\n- Risk scores, advance directives, consents\n\nThe coverage goes well beyond USCDI. The 218-field claim information appendix alone demonstrates a level of billing data detail that most vendors don't approach. The View product's 87 entities with 12 dedicated billing/insurance tables (286 fields) further reinforce the breadth. The only meaningful gaps are in structured imaging data and specialty-specific clinical entities (which are likely captured generically through flowsheets and questionnaires).\n\n**Axis 2 — Export approach: Purpose-built EHI export**\n\nClear signals this is purpose-built for (b)(10):\n\n1. **Native database model**: The EHR export uses internal database table names (DEMOGRAPHICS, HX_DIAGNOSIS, MEDICATIONS, MEDADMIN_RECORD, etc.) and SQL types — this is a direct database-level export, not a standards projection.\n2. **EHI-specific data**: Includes data that would never appear in (g)(10) or C-CDA: internal patient IDs, revision numbers, flowsheet definitions, risk scores, contact chunks, chart attachments, VIP indicators, organ donor flags, electronically-acquired-vital flags.\n3. **Separate from FHIR API**: The FMH guide explicitly states \"This is not an implementation of SMART/HL7 Bulk Data Access (Flat FHIR). FollowMyHealth is not currently using any FHIR Profile, such as US Core in this implementation.\"\n4. **Dedicated billing export**: The PM product has a separate, purpose-built billing data export that doesn't exist in any standard clinical exchange.\n5. **Five-product coverage**: Rather than pointing at a single FHIR API, Veradigm documents separate exports for each product component, each in its native format.\n6. **Active development**: The View documentation has been updated 6 times since April 2025.\n\n### Key Findings\n\n1. **Breadth across the suite is exceptional**: 169 entities and 2,938 fields spanning clinical, billing, messaging, documents, and portal data across 5 product components. This is among the most comprehensive EHI export documentation in the ambulatory EHR market.\n\n2. **Billing data is genuinely deep**: The Practice Management export documents 392 billing-related fields including specialty appendices for dental, ambulance, anesthesia, and drug billing. The View product adds 12 billing/insurance entities with 286 fields including 70-field superbill and 65-field insurance tables. This goes well beyond typical \"we export billing\" claims.\n\n3. **Database-level export, not a clinical summary repackaging**: The EHR export maps directly to 51 internal database tables with SQL types and primary keys. Fields like `RevisionNumber`, `ContactId`, `ActiveStatusFlag`, `VIPIndicator`, and `ElectronicallyAcquiredWeightFlag` are clearly from the native database, not a standards projection.\n\n4. **Documentation quality is high but aging for the core EHR**: The EHR PDF (v1, Nov 2023) hasn't been updated despite 2+ years of product development and a new version certification. The View documentation (v6, Jan 2026) is actively maintained. There are no sample data files or machine-readable schemas.\n\n5. **The five-product architecture creates fragmentation**: A recipient must handle JSON, TSV, and FHIR R4 formats, and there's no single export that covers the full patient record. The EHR export is clinical-focused; billing requires the PM export; insurance detail requires ePrescribe; portal data requires FMH. There's overlap (demographics appear in all products) but also gaps between products that aren't documented.\n\n### Summary Stats\n\n```\nCoverage:        Comprehensive\nApproach:        Purpose-built EHI export\nExport format:   JSON (EHR, PM), TSV (ePrescribe, View), FHIR R4 (FMH)\nEntities:        169 (51 EHR + 6 ePrescribe + 7 PM + 18 FMH + 87 View)\nFields:          2,938\nDescriptions:    99.9% of fields have descriptions\nSample data:     No\nBulk export:     Unclear (multi-patient supported; no documented bulk API)\nDomains covered: 18 of 19 applicable domains (imaging is partial)\n```\n\n### Bottom Line\n\nA patient or provider using the full Veradigm suite would get a detailed, database-level copy of their clinical, billing, messaging, and portal data across 169 documented entities and 2,938 fields. The export is genuinely purpose-built for (b)(10) — it exposes internal database tables, billing claims, and EHR-specific metadata far beyond what any FHIR API or C-CDA exchange would cover. The biggest practical challenge is the fragmented five-product architecture requiring multiple export mechanisms and formats. Product Context\n\nVeradigm EHR (formerly Allscripts Professional EHR) is a full-featured ambulatory EHR for small-to-mid-size independent physician practices and multi-specialty organizations. It is the flagship clinical product of Veradigm Inc. (formerly Allscripts Healthcare Solutions), with ~180,000 physician users and approximately 3.6% of the U.S. ambulatory EHR market.\n\nThe product ecosystem includes several separately sold but integrated products:\n\n- **Veradigm EHR** — the ONC-certified clinical EHR (the subject of this analysis, CHPL 11763)\n- **Veradigm Practice Management** — billing, claims, scheduling (separately sold, non-ONC-certified)\n- **Veradigm ePrescribe** — standalone electronic prescribing (also available as a module within the EHR)\n- **FollowMyHealth** — patient portal and personal health record (separately ONC-certified)\n- **Veradigm View** — rebranded Practice Fusion EHR, a simpler cloud-native EHR for small practices\n\n**What the product stores (relevant to export completeness):**\n- Full clinical documentation including one-click templates, specialty-specific protocols, ambient AI-generated notes\n- ePrescribing with EPCS, PDMP integration, prior authorization (eAUTH), medication pricing\n- Lab and imaging orders/results via the DORN network (500+ labs/radiology centers)\n- Clinical decision support, HCC alerts, risk scores\n- Immunization records and public health reporting data\n- Care plans, goals, health concerns, questionnaires\n- Patient communications and secure messaging\n- Scanned documents, transcriptions, chart attachments\n- Billing/claims data (via Practice Management), insurance, superbills\n- Patient portal data (via FollowMyHealth) including patient-entered data, appointment scheduling, billing\n\nThe ONC certification spans 40+ criteria including clinical (a)(1)-(a)(15), care coordination (b)(1)-(b)(11), quality measures (c)(1)-(c)(3), public health reporting (f)(1)-(f)(7), and FHIR APIs (g)(10).\n\n## 2. Published Nov 9, 2023. | **Highest** |\n| 2 | `veradigm-view-v6/*.html` (88 files) | ~20 MB total | **Veradigm View (Practice Fusion) data dictionary** — 87 TSV entity definitions, 1,194 fields. Export Mechanics\n\nVeradigm provides separate export mechanisms for each product component:\n\n**Veradigm EHR (core clinical data):**\n- **Format**: JSON files organized in clinical domain folders, plus raw attachments/documents/transcriptions\n- **Packaging**: Password-protected ZIP containing per-patient sub-ZIPs\n- **Mechanism**: EHI Export tool within the EHR application (UI-driven)\n- **Scope**: Single-patient or multi-patient export\n- **Access**: Practice initiates export; patient receives ZIP + password\n\n**Veradigm Practice Management (billing data):**\n- **Format**: Hierarchical JSON (single file per patient)\n- **Mechanism**: Not explicitly documented; described as \"EHI data export file\"\n- **Scope**: Per-patient financial/billing data\n- **Note**: PM is \"non ONC certified\" per the compliance page but provides separate EHI documentation\n\n**Veradigm ePrescribe (prescribing data):**\n- **Format**: TSV files in ZIP\n- **Mechanism**: Health Information Export tool within ePrescribe\n- **Scope**: Per-patient; supports single or multi-patient selection\n\n**FollowMyHealth (patient portal data):**\n- **Format**: FHIR R4 Bundle in JSON + raw documents/images in ZIP\n- **Mechanism**: Export from FMH Dashboard (by practice) or by patient from their PHR account\n- **Scope**: Per-patient; practice-initiated exports limited to data from that practice's EHR; patient-initiated exports include all sources\n- **Note**: Explicitly states \"This is not an implementation of SMART/HL7 Bulk Data Access (Flat FHIR)\"\n\n**Veradigm View / Practice Fusion (separate EHR):**\n- **Format**: TSV files\n- **Mechanism**: Not documented in the artifacts reviewed\n- **Scope**: 87 entity types across demographics, clinical, labs, billing, messaging, administrative domains\n\n**Bulk export capability**: Not explicitly documented as a single \"bulk export all patients\" mechanism. The EHR export supports multi-patient selection. No mention of fees or access constraints.\n\n## 4. |\n\nThe export also includes the actual binary files (images, scanned documents, transcriptions) in separate folders, not just metadata references.\n\n### 4b. Veradigm Practice Management\n\nThe PM export documents a hierarchical JSON structure for patient billing/financial data with **75 core fields** covering:\n- Practice and patient identification\n- Voucher-level billing data (charges, payments, adjustments, balances)\n- Provider, referring provider, responsible party, billing provider details\n- Service-level details (procedure codes, descriptions, units, fees, modifiers, diagnoses)\n- Payment transactions (date, insurance, transaction type, amount, transfers)\n\nPlus **317 appendix fields** covering possible values for:\n- **Claim information** (218 fields): prior authorization, condition codes 1-7, occurrence codes 1-8, value codes 1-12, diagnosis codes, procedure codes, employer info, scan regions, outgoing referrals, EPSDT fields, and more\n- **Ailment information** (51 fields): case type, disability dates, hospitalization dates, pregnancy-related, EPSDT referral codes\n- **Ambulance information** (21 fields): transport codes, pick-up addresses, stretcher/emergency indicators\n- **Drug information** (13 fields): NDC codes, lot numbers, unit pricing, lab results\n- **Anesthesia information** (12 fields): start/stop times, base units, CRNA details, related procedures\n- **Dental information** (2 fields): tooth/quadrant, surface\n\n### 4c. It is a separate product from Veradigm EHR (Practice Fusion rebranded), but its inclusion on the same compliance page reflects the integrated suite approach.\n\n## 5. Coverage Assessment\n\n### 5a. What the vendor covers (bottom-up)\n\n**Veradigm EHR** covers the core clinical data comprehensively:\n- **Demographics** (124 fields across 4 tables): exceptionally detailed including multiple name variants (preferred, former, birth), multiple sex/gender fields (birth sex, medical sex, administrative sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, preferred pronouns), organ donor status, employment, VIP indicator, confidentiality codes.\n- **Medications** (100 fields across 3 tables): active prescriptions with 58 fields including local vs. mail-order pharmacy details, sample drug tracking, MAR records with injection sites and lot numbers.\n- **Encounter** (94 fields across 7 tables): encounters, assessments, plans, HPI data, addenda, accompanied-by records.\n- **History** (87 fields across 3 tables): historical diagnoses, historical medications, implantable devices with UDI/DI codes.\n- **Messages** (72 fields across 3 tables): saved messages, web messages, and message results.\n- **Immunization** (59 fields across 4 tables): immunization records, VIS editions, forecast, and addenda.\n- **Additional Files** (67 fields across 4 tables plus actual files): scanned documents, transcriptions, chart attachments with metadata.\n\n**Practice Management** adds deep billing coverage:\n- 75 core fields covering the full voucher-to-payment lifecycle\n- 218 claim information fields covering institutional, professional, and specialty billing\n- Specialty appendices for ambulance, anesthesia, dental, and drug billing\n\n**Combined across the suite**, the strongest areas are:\n1. **Billing/insurance** — PM provides extensive claim-level detail; View has 12 billing entities with 286 fields; ePrescribe adds 40 insurance fields\n2. **Medications/prescriptions** — Three products cover active prescriptions, historical medications, administered medications, and prescription transactions\n3. **Demographics** — All products include patient demographics at varying depths\n4. **Clinical notes/documents** — EHR exports actual files (images, scanned docs, transcriptions, voice notes) plus metadata\n\n### 5b. The data should still be exported, but without specialty-specific documentation, it's hard to verify coverage.\n\n2. **Prior authorization records**: The ePrescribe product has eAUTH for electronic prior authorization, but no dedicated prior authorization entity appears in the EHR export. The PM export includes \"Prior Authorization Number\" as a claim field.\n\n3. **Structured imaging data**: No dedicated radiology or DICOM entities. Imaging data appears to come through as attachments and procedure results.\n\n4. **Patient-generated data from FollowMyHealth**: Remote monitoring device data is mentioned in product features but not specifically documented as an exported data type beyond FMH's Observation resource.\n\nThese are relatively minor gaps for an ambulatory EHR. The core clinical, billing, messaging, and document data are well-covered.\n\n## 6. Documentation Quality\n\n**Strengths:**\n- **Field-level documentation is excellent**: 99.9% of fields across all products have human-readable descriptions (2,935 of 2,938 fields). 100% have data types.\n- **Database-level transparency**: EHR export documentation names the actual database table and primary key for each JSON file, enabling developers to understand the data model\n- **SQL types provided**: VARCHAR(255), Integer, DateTime, etc. — not just \"string\" or \"text\"\n- **Multiple format options**: JSON (EHR, PM), TSV (ePrescribe, View), FHIR R4 (FMH) — all documented\n- **Versioning**: View documentation has been updated 6 times (v1 Apr 2025 through v6 Jan 2026); PM and FMH each have v2 revisions\n- **FHIR extension definitions**: FMH provides machine-readable StructureDefinitions, CodeSystems, and ValueSets for custom extensions\n\n**Weaknesses:**\n- **EHR documentation is dated**: Only v1 from November 2023 despite the product being certified at version 26 in December 2025. The documentation references \"Veradigm EHR 23.4 and higher\" — 2+ years of product updates are undocumented.\n- **No sample data**: None of the products provide sample export files or example records\n- **No machine-readable schema**: No JSON Schema, XSD, or other parseable schema definition — just PDF and HTML documentation\n- **No explicit relationship documentation**: Foreign keys between tables (PatientID, EncounterId, ContactId) are implied by field descriptions but not formally specified\n- **No value set definitions**: Coded fields like PatientMaritalStatus, Race, Ethnicity are documented as VARCHAR(255) with no enumeration of allowed values. The asterisk convention \"(*) means Other\" appears in some fields but many coded fields have no value sets.\n- **Five separate export mechanisms**: A receiving system must implement five different format parsers (JSON, TSV, FHIR R4) to consume the full patient record across all products\n\n**Could a developer build an import?** Yes, with significant effort. The field-level documentation is sufficient to understand the data model. The main challenges would be: (1) handling five different formats, (2) discovering value sets empirically, and (3) resolving relationships between tables across products.\n\n## 7. Overall Assessment\n\n### Classification\n\n**Axis 1 — Coverage breadth: Comprehensive**\n\nThis is one of the most comprehensive EHI export documentation suites among ambulatory EHR vendors. The combined documentation covers:\n- 169 entities with 2,938 fields across 5 products\n- All major clinical domains (demographics, problems, medications, labs, vitals, immunizations, procedures, encounters, care plans)\n- Billing and claims data at a deep level (PM export with 392 fields including specialty billing appendices)\n- Insurance with PBM detail (ePrescribe Insurance.tsv with 40 fields)\n- Patient communications (45-field message table, web messages, FMH Communication resource)\n- Actual binary files (images, scanned documents, transcriptions) — not just metadata\n- Patient portal data (FMH FHIR export with 18 resource types)\n- Questionnaires and flowsheets (generic containers that capture specialty data)\n- Risk scores, advance directives, consents\n\nThe coverage goes well beyond USCDI. The 218-field claim information appendix alone demonstrates a level of billing data detail that most vendors don't approach. The View product's 87 entities with 12 dedicated billing/insurance tables (286 fields) further reinforce the breadth. The only meaningful gaps are in structured imaging data and specialty-specific clinical entities (which are likely captured generically through flowsheets and questionnaires).\n\n**Axis 2 — Export approach: Purpose-built EHI export**\n\nClear signals this is purpose-built for (b)(10):\n\n1. **Native database model**: The EHR export uses internal database table names (DEMOGRAPHICS, HX_DIAGNOSIS, MEDICATIONS, MEDADMIN_RECORD, etc.) and SQL types — this is a direct database-level export, not a standards projection.\n2. **EHI-specific data**: Includes data that would never appear in (g)(10) or C-CDA: internal patient IDs, revision numbers, flowsheet definitions, risk scores, contact chunks, chart attachments, VIP indicators, organ donor flags, electronically-acquired-vital flags.\n3. **Separate from FHIR API**: The FMH guide explicitly states \"This is not an implementation of SMART/HL7 Bulk Data Access (Flat FHIR). FollowMyHealth is not currently using any FHIR Profile, such as US Core in this implementation.\"\n4. **Dedicated billing export**: The PM product has a separate, purpose-built billing data export that doesn't exist in any standard clinical exchange.\n5. **Five-product coverage**: Rather than pointing at a single FHIR API, Veradigm documents separate exports for each product component, each in its native format.\n6. **Active development**: The View documentation has been updated 6 times since April 2025.\n\n### Key Findings\n\n1. **Breadth across the suite is exceptional**: 169 entities and 2,938 fields spanning clinical, billing, messaging, documents, and portal data across 5 product components. This is among the most comprehensive EHI export documentation in the ambulatory EHR market.\n\n2. **Billing data is genuinely deep**: The Practice Management export documents 392 billing-related fields including specialty appendices for dental, ambulance, anesthesia, and drug billing. The View product adds 12 billing/insurance entities with 286 fields including 70-field superbill and 65-field insurance tables. This goes well beyond typical \"we export billing\" claims.\n\n3. **Database-level export, not a clinical summary repackaging**: The EHR export maps directly to 51 internal database tables with SQL types and primary keys. Fields like `RevisionNumber`, `ContactId`, `ActiveStatusFlag`, `VIPIndicator`, and `ElectronicallyAcquiredWeightFlag` are clearly from the native database, not a standards projection.\n\n4. **Documentation quality is high but aging for the core EHR**: The EHR PDF (v1, Nov 2023) hasn't been updated despite 2+ years of product development and a new version certification. The View documentation (v6, Jan 2026) is actively maintained. There are no sample data files or machine-readable schemas.\n\n5. **The five-product architecture creates fragmentation**: A recipient must handle JSON, TSV, and FHIR R4 formats, and there's no single export that covers the full patient record. The EHR export is clinical-focused; billing requires the PM export; insurance detail requires ePrescribe; portal data requires FMH.
